name: Highlands 19

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, with dense juniper and conifer tree cover dominating the entire frontage and surrounding terrain|The residence is largely obscured by vegetation from this front perspective, with only a small visible structure near the center of the view|A paved roadway runs along the bottom of the frame, providing the primary street access to the property|The heavy tree screening along the front significantly limits visibility of the structure and driveway entrance from the street.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property set within a heavily wooded desert landscape dominated by juniper-type conifers and open sandy terrain|The residence and associated structures are not clearly visible from this perspective due to dense tree screening on the right flank|The road visible at the far right edge confirms street access along this side of the property|No fencing, outbuildings, or secondary access routes are visible from this angle.

charlie.desc: The charlie view reveals the rear of the property from a distance, with the main residence partially visible as a low-profile, earth-toned structure near the center of the frame surrounded by dense conifers|The structure has a multi-segment roofline consistent with a spread-out single-story residence|Dense tree cover on all sides of the rear yard severely limits responder visibility and movement routes to the back of the structure|No rear driveway, gate, or secondary access point is visible from this perspective.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with dense conifer and juniper tree cover extending across the entire visible terrain|A paved road is visible along the left edge of the frame, confirming street access on this side|The residence is partially discernible as a light-colored structure set back from the road, screened heavily by surrounding trees|No secondary structures, fencing, or access routes are clearly identifiable from the left side.

considerations: The residence sits on a heavily wooded desert lot with dense juniper and conifer tree cover on all sides, significantly limiting visibility and responder approach from any direction. The single paved driveway visible in the nadir image provides the primary — and observably the only — vehicular access point to the structure, with a curved approach through vegetation. A sport court and a detached structure are visible to the north of the main residence. The long, curved driveway and dense tree screening on all perimeter sides will constrain staging options and limit aerial and ground-level sightlines to the structure.
clarifications: Is the driveway entrance from Macalpine Loop gated or controlled, and if so, what is the access method? What is the surface material and load-bearing capacity of the driveway for heavy emergency vehicles? Are there any secondary pedestrian or vehicle access routes through the perimeter vegetation? Is there a Knox Box or other emergency access provision at the drive entrance? Are any propane or other fuel storage tanks located on the property?
